items.followUp: Define a covalent compound and state three of its properties.

rubric.why: The definition should describe electron transfer and the formation of oppositely charged ions.
rubric.how: Award for stating that electron transfer forms oppositely charged ions held together by electrostatic attraction.

rubric.why: Strong attractions between ions require considerable heat to overcome.
rubric.how: Award for stating that ionic compounds have high melting points or high boiling points.

rubric.why: Ions can move freely and carry charge when the compound is molten or dissolved in water.
rubric.description: Conduct electricity when molten or dissolved in water.
rubric.how: Award for stating that molten ionic compounds or their aqueous solutions conduct electricity.

rubric.why: Many ionic compounds dissolve in water.
rubric.how: Award for stating that ionic compounds are generally soluble in water.

modelAnswer: Ionic compounds are formed by the transfer of electrons from one atom to another, producing oppositely charged ions held together by electrostatic attraction.
They usually have high melting points and high boiling points.
They are usually soluble in water.
They conduct electricity when molten or dissolved in water, but not in the solid state.

items.followUp: Explain why a liquid with stronger intermolecular forces generally has a higher boiling point.

rubric.why: Boiling point varies according to the nature of the liquid.
rubric.description: Boiling point depends on the nature of the liquid.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the boiling point depends on the nature of the liquid.

rubric.why: Stronger attractions between particles are associated with a higher boiling point.
rubric.description: Stronger intermolecular forces give a higher boiling point.
rubric.how: Award for correctly linking stronger intermolecular forces with a higher boiling point.

rubric.why: The answer should connect the higher boiling point with the energy needed to overcome attractions between particles.
rubric.description: More heat is needed to overcome stronger intermolecular forces.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that extra heat or energy is needed to overcome the forces or separate the particles.

rubric.why: Weaker attractions are overcome more easily, so less heating is needed for boiling.
rubric.description: Weaker intermolecular forces give a lower boiling point.
rubric.how: Award for correctly linking weaker intermolecular forces with a lower boiling point.

modelAnswer: The boiling point depends on the nature of the liquid and the strength of the forces between its particles.
A liquid with stronger intermolecular forces has a higher boiling point because more heat is needed to overcome those forces and separate the particles.
A liquid with weaker intermolecular forces has a lower boiling point because less heat is needed to separate its particles.

items.followUp: State one limitation of Rutherford’s atomic model concerning the stability of atoms.

rubric.why: Rutherford’s model could not explain why electrons do not lose energy and collapse into the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the model predicted orbiting electrons would lose energy and fall into the nucleus, making atoms unstable.

rubric.why: The model did not account for the discrete spectra of atoms.
rubric.description: Failure to explain atomic line spectra.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the model could not explain the line spectra of atoms.

modelAnswer: Rutherford’s model could not explain the stability of the atom: orbiting electrons should radiate energy and fall into the nucleus.
It could not explain the discrete line spectra of atoms or the arrangement of electrons around the nucleus.

items.followUp: Name one radioactive isotope used to treat cancer and state its use.

rubric.why: Cobalt 60 is a radioisotope used in radiotherapy.
Iodine 131 is used to treat thyroid disorders, including thyroid cancer.

modelAnswer: Cobalt 60 is used in radiotherapy to treat cancer.
Iodine 131 is also used to treat thyroid disorders, including thyroid cancer.

items.followUp: State how the long-form periodic table is arranged and give its number of groups.

rubric.why: The long-form periodic table orders elements by atomic number.
rubric.how: Award for stating that elements are arranged in order of increasing atomic number.

rubric.why: The long-form periodic table has 18 vertical groups and 7 horizontal periods.
rubric.description: Groups or periods in the table.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the table has 18 groups or 7 periods.

modelAnswer: In the long-form periodic table, elements are arranged in order of increasing atomic number.
It has 18 vertical groups and 7 horizontal periods.
